title: Crème Brûlée
subtitle: Baked vanilla cream with a caramel crust
excerpt: Egg yolk and double cream custard baked in a bain-marie until barely set, then chilled and finished with a layer of caster sugar caramelised to a brittle toffee crust with a blowtorch.

recipe.sourceNotes: Crème brûlée is a classic French dessert, though its origin is contested between France, England, and Spain. The English version, 'burnt cream', was recorded at Trinity College, Cambridge in the 17th century. The French name became standard in English restaurants in the 20th century. The defining feature is the contrast of the cold, barely-set custard below and the brittle, hot caramel crust above. The custard is made from cream and egg yolks only, with no flour, milk, or cornflour — this gives it a silky, almost trembling texture. A culinary blowtorch is the most reliable way to achieve an even caramel crust.

content.text: The custard is done when it has a very slight wobble in the centre: it will firm up considerably as it cools. Overbaked custard will be grainy and curdled. The bain-marie insulates the ramekins from direct heat and gives a more even bake. The custard must be completely cold before adding the sugar and caramelising: a warm custard will melt rather than brulee.
Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Place 6 ramekins in a deep roasting tin. Bring the cream just to the point of simmering in a saucepan. Remove from the heat.
Whisk the egg yolks with the 60 g caster sugar and vanilla until pale. Pour the hot cream over slowly, whisking constantly. Strain through a sieve into a jug.

Pour the custard into the ramekins. Pour enough hot water into the roasting tin to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the centre.
Remove from the bain-marie and cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of caster sugar evenly over each custard. Use a blowtorch to caramelise the sugar until it forms a deep amber, bubbling crust. Leave for 1 minute before serving.
